Q: How does the Operating System find the best area for heap? A:

Multitasking systems are usually working with paging, so not in real mode.

MS-DOS was in real-mode but single-task, launching a new process started where the last one ended.

Is there a real-mode multitasking system? Hmmm, what about minix? Basically processes get assigned memory in "segments" and the memory of one process may be split into multiple separate segments residing in different memory locations.

Q: Beginner building Scraping/Crawling Workflow A:

I'd recommend using Apache Solr and Nutch for the web crawling. Solr is a search/indexing platform and Nutch is a web crawler that can filter out the HTML content and store it inside of Solr. Both of these can be spun up using docker containers so that you don't actually need to write any code to do the web crawling. You can configure Nutch to begin a web crawl from each university landing page and then download all of the extracted content from Solr. Once you have that content you can feed it into your own scripts, and focus on writing code to search for the desired requirements using LLMs or whatever kind of filtering you think would be best.

Writing web-crawlers is a challenging project to get right and the Solr/Nutch combo is a free, professional-grade approach to it.

On a side note, I'd imagine that the math requirements for electrical engineering degrees are largely consistent across universities: calculus, differential equations, and signals/Fourier analysis.

Q: How can I install the 'os' module? A:

Q: What can I do to make my TOF sensor work? A:

All HAL functions for I2C peripherals which take an address parameter expect you to shift the address left by one bit before passing it into the function.

e.g. here's the comment above the function HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit():

/**
  * @brief  Transmits in master mode an amount of data in blocking mode.
  * @param  hi2c Pointer to a I2C_HandleTypeDef structure that contains
  *                the configuration information for the specified I2C.
  * @param  DevAddress Target device address: The device 7 bits address value
  *         in datasheet must be shifted to the left before calling the interface
  * @param  pData Pointer to data buffer
  * @param  Size Amount of data to be sent
  * @param  Timeout Timeout duration
  * @retval HAL status
  */

Note the comment for the DevAddress parameter: The device 7 bits address value in datasheet must be shifted to the left before calling the interface.

So you'll need to change all function calls that pass an I2C address to do this shift. i.e. change:

HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit(hi2c, VL53L0X_ADDRESS, &reg, 1, 100);

to

HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit(hi2c, VL53L0X_ADDRESS << 1, &reg, 1, 100);

and similar for each function call.

There may be other issues, but this is certainly part of the problem.
